There was a vaguely similar study done several years ago. Women were shown photos of men standing next to or sitting in mid-range cars, other women were shown pictures of the same men standing next to or sitting in expensive luxury or sports cars. The women were asked to solely rate the physical attractiveness of the men. The results showed that women consistently rated the men as more physically attractive when they were next to expensive cars.

A parallel study with men looking at photos of women with mid-range and expensive cars showed that the cars had no effect on the women's perceived physical attractiveness.

The point being that environmental factors can skew perceived physical attractiveness.
